GNU/Linux on Desmos

A RISC-V (RV32IMA, Sv32 MMU) computer built entirely from Desmos expressions, running the Linux kernel with GNU bash, GNU coreutils and the GNU C library.

Press the ▶ play button on the ticker (top of this list) to power on. Booting to a shell prompt takes over an hour; the console shows kernel messages as they arrive. Type with the on-screen keyboard below the terminal (Shift and Ctrl apply to the next key).

How it works: each tick, the ticker action A_t runs thousands of CPU steps through a recursive Desmos function. Memory stores go to a write log, which A_t then merges into the RAM page lists (folder "RAM"). The console is an SBI firmware call implemented by the CPU; its output feeds a VT100-style terminal emulator, drawn with a Hershey vector font.
k_o = chains of 5000 CPU steps per tick. Raise it for more speed if your computer keeps up; lower it if the page becomes unresponsive.
